validation_results.peer_auth_model: HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-001 section 10 / PAWAH-INV-8 -- VERIFIED. Before admitting any operation the helper obtains the kernel-authenticated OS (uid, gid[, pid]) of the channel peer (SO_PEERCRED / LOCAL_PEERCRED / getpeereid profiles -- not assumed byte-for-byte equivalent), NOT from any peer-supplied protocol field, and requires: peer uid is the deployment-owner OS principal (resolved from the filesystem, not the request) AND peer uid is NOT the configured agent principal AND the credential is bound to the actual channel AND on the two-principal topology the accounts are distinct, and where the topology is absent -> REAL issuance ineligible, fail closed. A required conjunct, evaluated BEFORE operation admission and BEFORE any protected-store read. OS peer credential != human identity != human approval != informed intent. A claimed UID / GID / PID inside JSON cannot satisfy the requirement
validation_results.anti_toctou_property: HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-REQ-029 / section 33C VerifiedExecutionObjectValid -- VERIFIED. The helper that is executed SHALL be the same file object whose integrity / ownership / type properties the launcher verified -- validation and execution address one opened descriptor (or a platform-equivalent identity-preserving handle); a pathname re-open after validation is forbidden. verify(path A) then execute(A via a fresh pathname resolution) is rejected. The contract freezes the PROPERTY; the concrete syscall (fexecve, execveat with AT_EMPTY_PATH, or a documented platform equivalent) is an implementation profile. A platform that cannot execute the verified object without a substitution window STOPS BLOCKED -- not downgraded. The contract distinguishes the logical assurance property from the platform implementation profile and does not require a specific syscall. Feasible on the macOS development host and the Linux (Dell Ubuntu) deployment target; the 'platform-equivalent' wording is always paired with an explicit BLOCKED alternative -- no infeasibility papered over
validation_results.configured_agent_identity_rule: HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-REQ-032 / section 33C ConfiguredAgentIdentityBindingValid (finding F-1 / F-5-B1, preserved and executed inside the helper) -- VERIFIED. The helper process principal is the deployment owner and MAY run with elevated (sudo / root EUID) privilege; the negative boundary (step 3 / step 7) SHALL still be evaluated against the configured PCAE agent principal resolved live from HPAC-PAWA-AGENT-EXCLUSION/1.0 -- never os.geteuid(), an ambient root EUID, a SUDO_ variable, or a caller parameter. euid == 0 inside the helper mints nothing. validation_results.freshness_and_replay_model: HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-001 section 18 / section 19 -- VERIFIED. Every request carries expiry (trusted-clock) + per-request CSPRNG nonce >= 256 bits; the helper validates freshness against its own trusted clock; past expiry -> fail closed (capability_stale) regardless of every other conjunct. The helper distinguishes and treats distinctly: fresh (admit once) / consumed (DENY -- cannot be accepted again even if its response was lost) / duplicate (DENY -- at most one helper process may admit a given (request_id, nonce)) / expired (DENY) / unknown (DENY operation_scope_invalid) / conflicting replay (a (request_id, nonce) reused with different operation / session_id / subject -> DENY target_scope_invalid). A lost response does not make the original request unused -- once a one-shot op crosses MUTATION_ATTEMPT_STARTED its (request_id, nonce) is spent; the caller reconciles against the protected-root evidence record, does not resend. A request id or nonce is not itself authority. certification_read is idempotent (fresh helper, full recognition per call). receipt = evidence != authority; response absence != proof no mutation happened
validation_results.state_transition_and_uncertainty_model: HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-001 section 20 / section 21 -- VERIFIED. Frozen ordered model REQUEST_RECEIVED -> REQUEST_AUTHENTICATED -> OPERATION_ADMITTED -> MUTATION_ATTEMPT_STARTED -> MUTATION_COMMITTED -> EVIDENCE_WRITTEN -> RESPONSE_EMITTED. What each transition proves / does not prove is frozen (MUTATION_ATTEMPT_STARTED != MUTATION_COMMITTED; MUTATION_COMMITTED != RESPONSE_EMITTED / observed; RESPONSE_EMITTED != caller received / human observed). Durable transitions (survive a crash, reconcilable from the protected root): MUTATION_COMMITTED and EVIDENCE_WRITTEN; the earlier states are process-local and leave no protected-root effect. No automatic retry once MUTATION_ATTEMPT_STARTED is crossed unless the operation contract proves the mutation idempotent or reconcilable; the no-auto-retry boundary begins at the correct point. The section 21 crash table covers every material stage; a crash after MUTATION_COMMITTED before EVIDENCE_WRITTEN -> INDETERMINATE / RECONCILIATION REQUIRED (deployment-owner reconciliation finalizes or quarantines) -- never reported as success, never auto-retried; response loss is never proof the mutation did not happen; unknown outcome remains unknown until reconciled against the durable protected-root evidence record
validation_results.audit_write_ordering: HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-REQ-086 -- VERIFIED (model A). Evidence durably staged BEFORE the mutation, finalized AFTER commit: (1) before MUTATION_ATTEMPT_STARTED the helper durably writes a state='staged' record binding request digest / operation / role / session / subject / nonce / expiry; (2) staged-write failure -> abort before any mutation, fail closed (internal_fail_closed); (3) the helper performs the one mutation; (4) the helper finalizes the staged record (state='committed' + committed-record digest) = EVIDENCE_WRITTEN; (5) a crash between (3) and (4) -> the INDETERMINATE / RECONCILIATION REQUIRED state. HPAC-PAWA-HELPER-REQ-087: the contract does NOT claim 'audit-write failure means the mutation did not occur' unconditionally -- it guarantees the ordering that makes a pre-mutation staged-evidence failure abort before any mutation, and a post-commit finalization failure a detectable reconciliation condition rather than a silent success. An explicit reconciliation / indeterminate disposition exists for the commit / finalize gap
validation_results.non_bearer_restart_dead: section 49C / PAWAH-INV-10 -- VERIFIED. Sections 45 to 49 / 49A / 49B become properties of the helper-process boundary -- no returnable authority object to serialise / copy / capture; the helper process (and any capability it minted internally) is gone at exit; a restart cannot revive stale consumed authority; a fresh launch re-runs the entire section 33C + section 33 1-8 recognition; a lost response never frees a spent one-shot (request_id, nonce). Authority is operation-specific, one-shot where specified, non-serialisable as a generic capability, dead when the helper exits, not revived by process restart / response loss, not recreated from typed evidence. A fresh process repeats the full trust / admission sequence
validation_results.single_trust_root: PAWA-INV-17 / PAWAH-INV-7 -- VERIFIED.
